\begin{abstract}
Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation can answer a document question from optical character
recognition (OCR) text, from a retrieved page image, or from both, at different GPU cost. Serving it at scale is
a GPU provisioning problem: generation compute grows with the request rate, and late-interaction visual indexes grow
with the corpus, to about 246\,GiB at a million pages. We present the Cost-Aware Visual Router (CAVR), which
chooses the answer path per query with a run-time cost weight. On one RTX 4090, we run every path on
8,150 DocVQA and InfographicVQA questions with one shared generator and answer quality as average normalised Levenshtein similarity (ANLS), GPU-seconds, energy and latency. A
content-aware router, CAVR-CE, whose cross-encoder (CE) reads the retrieved passages before generation, uses
29\% less GPU compute than always using both contexts, at 0.008 lower mean ANLS, and 20\%
less than a quality-blind mix of the visual and hybrid paths at equal ANLS. In a load test simulated from
measured service times, it cuts the GPUs needed for 100 queries/s at a p95 latency of 2\,s from 106 to
72; always using the page image alone needs 64 at lower ANLS. Route labels derived
from question keywords agree with measured outcomes no better than chance. On two further GPU nodes, index sharding
scales near-linearly, and an index of a million pages held in host memory is searched by two GPUs in large
batches at close to the GPU cost per query of GPU-resident search, but takes seconds per single query.
\end{abstract}
